title: Robots that build robots
subtitle: Bootstrapping a Dyson sphere from first principles
author: Cam Pedersen
description: The Municipal Robotics vision: an autonomous company, amplified by intelligence. Software first, then arms that build arms, from a desk to a swarm of collectors around a star.

title: Gate-Pinned State Memory
subtitle: Exact storage in a model's recurrent state, and how far a model gets using it
author: Cam Pedersen
description: Gate-Pinned State Memory (GPSM) makes a Gated DeltaNet head exact RAM. We verified it bitwise from tang's kernel to a CUDA window in our engine, then measured it as agent memory: the storage is exact, but a model driving it recalled less than retrieval, or no memory at all.

title: Real-time, In-Body Talk
subtitle: A small streaming voice, trained in one tensor IR
author: Cam Pedersen
description: RIBT is a 54M-parameter streaming English TTS system whose networks are tang tensor-IR programs running on Metal, CUDA and WebGPU. It produces first audio 17.6 ms after receiving text on an M4 Max, against 349 ms for Kokoro-82M. Its voice is distilled from Kokoro's af_heart.

title: Seeing Is Measuring
subtitle: Editable CAD programs from photographs
author: Cam Pedersen
description: Editable CAD programs recovered from photographs through irys, and when to trust them. On held-out synthetic parts the fit's error bars and residual checks barely tell right answers from wrong ones; recovering again with one more photograph and flagging the part when its features change catches three in four wrong answers with few false alarms.

title: Differentiable Rendering with Exact Replay
subtitle: irys, an open-source spectral path tracer
author: Cam Pedersen
description: irys is an open-source spectral path tracer. Its backward pass replays the forward pass bit for bit, so two runs give identical gradients. We check those gradients against an f64 reference, and vcad's BRep kernel pulls them back to the dimensions of a CAD part.

title: Don't Write Kernels, Derive Them
subtitle: Chasing the Speed of Light: Kernels from a Tensor IR of Views and Comprehensions
author: Cam Pedersen
description: tang's tensor IR has two constructs, affine views and monoid comprehensions. Fusion, flash attention and its backward pass are derived as rewrites, and one graph lowers to CUDA, Metal, WGSL, OpenCL, GLSL and C. The least memory traffic and the optimal tile are dual solutions of one linear program, and a time floor built on it never exceeds measured time on the kernels we checked against hardware counters. Wins and losses against PyTorch, llama.cpp and FlashAttention are both reported.
